overview: 22 official Group 1 Qs (2008–2024) on population, sex ratio, SC/ST, tribes and races, languages and urbanisation. Almost all are one-liners on a census figure, rank or 'where is this group'; 2023–24 added match lists (sex ratios, nomadic tribes) and a negative language item. Population facts (8 Qs) lead; occupational structure, rural–urban components and migration are not yet asked. Several old keys use dated or near figures (ST 2001, AP rank 2011), so tie every number to its census.

possibility.angle: Population distribution, density and growth – world, India, AP
possibility.what_they_ask: census launch date, most/least populous or dense state/UT by census year, densest Latin American country, rate of natural increase from CBR/CDR, world population milestones
states/UTs with more females, NFHS vs Census sex ratio of AP, sex-ratio values matched to states
natural targets by analogy with the census items: Census 2011 main/marginal workers, cultivators vs agricultural labourers, work participation rate by sex and state
ST share of India, number of notified STs in AP, states/UTs with no SC population

possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs (one 2010 Q on rural share in Australia counted under population)
possibility.what_they_ask: natural targets: urban share (31.1% in 2011), most/least urbanised states, census town vs statutory town definition

possibility.angle: Racial, tribal, religious and linguistic groups
possibility.what_they_ask: tribe → region (Zulu, Hottentot, Pygmy, Masai, Semang, Punan), Shia-majority country, language family of an Indian language; other APPSC exams ask AP tribes and dances (e.g. Thimsa – Araku)
city nicknames and identities, main cause of urban growth in 2001–11 (reclassification)
natural targets: dominant stream (rural–rural), main reason for female migration (marriage), largest source and destination states, place of last residence concept

traps.trap: Shifts the ranking to another census year
traps.spot: Stem names a census (2001 or 2011) and the options include the leader of the other year
traps.fix: 2001 density: West Bengal > Bihar; 2011: Bihar > West Bengal

traps.trap: Gives a launch date, an enumeration date or a reference date in place of one another
traps.spot: Four dates in the same year
traps.fix: Census 2011: launched 1 April 2010 (houselisting); enumeration Feb 2011; reference date 1 March 2011

traps.trap: Moves a tribe to the neighbouring forest region
traps.spot: Match lists of equatorial hunters and pastoralists
traps.fix: Pygmies – Congo basin; Semang – Malay peninsula; Punan – Borneo; Masai – East Africa

traps.trap: Assigns a language to the wrong family
traps.fix: Dardic (Kashmiri, Shina) is Indo-Aryan, Indo-European; Sino-Tibetan is NE/Himalayan

traps.trap: Confuses herders with hunters of the same region
Picks the intuitive cause over the data-driven one
traps.spot: 'most important reason' for urban growth with migration as an option
traps.fix: In 2001–11 a large share of urban increase came from reclassification (new census towns)
traps.pyq: → categorisation of rural areas as urban [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#9]

traps.trap: Mixes a survey figure with a census figure
traps.spot: Sex ratio stem naming NFHS rather than Census

techniques.name: Rate arithmetic
techniques.how: Rate of natural increase (%) = (CBR − CDR) / 10, since both are per 1000. Watch the unit in options.

techniques.name: Milestone timeline
techniques.how: Keep the world population milestones: 1 bn 1804, 5 bn 1987, 6 bn 1999, 7 bn 2011, 8 bn 2022; match the interval in the stem.

techniques.name: Extreme-value anchoring in number matches
techniques.how: Fix the highest and lowest values first (Puducherry 1037 high, Lakshadweep 946 low), then the close pair (TN 996 vs AP 993).
techniques.example: Puducherry–1037 and Lakshadweep–946 leave only 'II III IV I' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#94]

techniques.name: Small-island density rule
techniques.how: For highest density in a region, prefer small islands or city-states over large countries.
techniques.example: Puerto Rico beats Brazil, Mexico, Panama [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#108]

techniques.name: Census-year tagging
techniques.how: Write the census year next to every figure you recall; reject options that are right for the other census.

confusions.remember: Bihar overtook WB in 2011 (1,106 vs 1,028 per sq km)
Houselisting starts a year before the count
Survey of households vs full count; AP 1020 vs 993
Herders vs hunters, both southern Africa
Congo forest hunters vs East African cattle herders
Dardic is Indo-Aryan; Sino-Tibetan is NE India, Ladakh, Sikkim
Santhali, Mundari, Ho in Jharkhand vs Telugu, Tamil, Gondi
Two of the three sources of urban growth (with migration)

Iran – the clearly Shia-majority state among common options
checklist: Which source and year – Census 2001, Census 2011 or NFHS?
Is the stem asking a launch, enumeration or reference date?
Check units (per 1000 vs %) before choosing a number
For tribe/race items, place the group in its exact forest or grassland region
For language items, name the family first, then the region
Where an old key uses a near figure, pick the option closest to the census value
